subject: Intermittent 5xxs from rw-chat-11B-v3 — production impact
messages:
From: Olivia Smith <olivia.smith@acme-retail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-platform-eng@acme-retail.com
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 5xxs from rw-chat-11B-v3 — production impact

Hi Jordan / Marcus,

We're seeing a spike of 5xx responses and client-side timeouts from rw-chat-11B-v3 starting ~07:45 UTC this morning. Error rate climbed from our baseline (~0.3%) to ~6% for user-facing generation endpoints. Impacting multiple storefronts — some sessions see immediate 5xx, others hang until client-side timeout (30s).

I've attached a small sample of failing request/response pairs and a short summary: response_samples_20260305.csv (2k rows, includes request_id). We can reproduce 5xxs hitting the model directly (same request that worked yesterday).

Can you confirm whether you see errors on your side and an ETA for a mitigation? We're currently throttling traffic to reduce user impact but need a plan for full recovery.

Thanks,
Olivia Smith
Platform Engineer — Acme Retail
olivia.smith@acme-retail.com

Attachments: response_samples_20260305.csv
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Smith <olivia.smith@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 5xxs from rw-chat-11B-v3 — production impact

Hi Olivia — thanks for the report and the samples. We see the same elevated 5xx/timeouts in our monitoring (alerts fired at 07:50 UTC). I've opened internal incident JIRA INF-3821 and escalated to infra/serving.

Short-term mitigation we are applying now:
- Route new traffic off rw-chat-11B-v3 to rw-chat-11B-v2 where possible (compatible API).
- Increase instance pool for the v3 fleet while we investigate to reduce contention.

I don't have a final ETA yet for full recovery; engineering is investigating a potential runtime regression. I'll update within the hour with more specifics.

Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Olivia Smith <olivia.smith@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 5xxs from rw-chat-11B-v3 — production impact

On Thu, Mar 5, 2026 at 09:01 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Olivia — thanks for the report and the samples. We see the same elevated 5xx/timeouts in our monitoring (alerts fired at 07:50 UTC). I've opened internal incident JIRA INF-3821 and escalated to infra/serving.

Quick technical update from infra: we're seeing a pattern of OOM-triggered process restarts tied to the new quantization kernel path that was enabled in the v3 rollout last week. The restart loop is producing transient 5xxs and some requests are hitting the pre-restart window where the KV cache isn't populated, causing long tail timeouts.

What we did at ~09:30 UTC:
- Disabled the new quantization kernel on v3 (rolled back to the previous kernel).
- Scoped traffic to healthy backends and spun up additional instances in the v2 pool to accept rerouted traffic.
- Collected targeted logs and heap profiles (attached: logs_20260305.tar.gz).

Status: error rate dropped from ~6% to ~1.2% in the 30 minutes after mitigation. There are still occasional timeouts likely from clients that were in-flight during restarts. We're keeping the rollback in place while we finish a deeper memory investigation.

Next steps (infra action items):
- Root cause analysis of memory regression in new kernel path (priority: P0).
- Hotfix for kernel memory accounting to prevent allocation spikes.
- Staged deployment plan for a tested kernel variant, with canary at 1% traffic before full rollout.

I'll join any customer call if you want to go through details.

Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachments: logs_20260305.tar.gz
From: Olivia Smith <olivia.smith@acme-retail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-platform-eng@acme-retail.com
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 5xxs from rw-chat-11B-v3 — production impact

Thanks for the quick response and the mitigation notes. We're seeing recovery on our side — rate of failures is back to ~0.9% and customer-facing errors are substantially reduced. A few sessions still recorded timeouts (likely the in-flight ones you mentioned).

We will keep throttling a subset of high-risk traffic until you confirm the kernel path is stable. Please let us know when you have the RCA and planned timeline for the permanent fix; we'll need that for our internal incident report.

Also: can you confirm whether Redwood will apply an incident credit for the window of elevated errors per our contract? I'll include that in the procurement thread if so.

Olivia

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Smith <olivia.smith@acme-retail.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — rw-chat-11B-v3 (INF-3821)

Hi Olivia (and Acme team),

Follow-up and post-incident summary for INF-3821. Thanks again for the quick report and for coordinating throttles during the mitigation window. Below is a concise timeline, root cause, impact, and mitigation + action items.

Timeline (UTC):
- 07:45 — First customer reports and internal alerts for elevated 5xx/timeouts.
- 07:50 — Monitoring alerting + initial triage.
- 09:30 — Infra rollback of new quantization kernel on rw-chat-11B-v3 and increased routing to rw-chat-11B-v2.
- 10:00 — Error rate fell to ~1.2%; continued slow tail of timeouts for in-flight requests.
- 12:00 — Customer reports recovery to ~0.9% error rate.

Root cause: regression in a newly enabled quantization execution path on rw-chat-11B-v3 that produced intermittent allocation spikes leading to process restarts and increased 5xxs. The behavior was not observed in earlier canary testing due to a workload distribution mismatch in our canary harness.

Impact: elevated 5xxs and timeouts for Acme Retail during the window 07:45–10:00 UTC on 2026-03-05. We estimate user-facing error rate peaked ~6% for affected endpoints.

Workarounds and mitigation applied: rollback of quantization kernel on v3, traffic routing to v2, and added instance capacity.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Marcus / Infra: complete memory accounting fix and validate with extended load tests (ETA: 2026-03-10).
- Engineering: add an expanded canary workload that mirrors enterprise traffic (ETA: 2026-03-17).
- Support / CS (Jordan): prepare a formal SLA credit proposal for affected window and share with procurement (ETA: 2026-03-09).
- All: postmortem doc published and shared (link below).

We will schedule a short call early next week to walk through the technical details if you'd like; Marcus will present the kernel fix plan.

Links & artifacts:
- JIRA: INF-3821
- Postmortem (internal + shared view): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-postmortem
- Collected logs/heap profiles: logs_20260305.tar.gz
- Sample requests/responses: response_samples_20260305.csv

Regarding credits: Jordan from CS will coordinate the SLA credit evaluation and get back to you with a formal calculation.

Apologies again for the disruption and thanks for your partnership while we remedied this.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
